title: Coalesce scheduler wake-ups before sending a full daemon prompt
evidence: Trace indicators count daemon-originated prompt deliveries per session and their character volume; each delivery can repeat goal/task status and handoff context. The database has no per-prompt usage, so this is a measured repetition indicator rather than measured token waste.
scope: Add a deduplicated pending-attention key at the scheduler/ACP delivery boundary. Preserve every distinct failure, user message, and explicit resume; do not change workflow columns, required checks, or prompt content for the first delivery.
benefit: Estimated reduction in repeated input context and avoidable wake-up latency; quantify only after instrumenting per-delivery counters.
measurement: On matched tasks, compare daemon prompt count, prompt characters, canonical uncached input, output, task lead time, and finish/review outcomes. Keep the same workflow and required checks.
counter_evidence: A wake-up may carry newly relevant state. If coalescing delays recovery, increases retries, or changes outcome quality, retain the existing behavior.

title: Measure and tighten handoff selection at the existing character budget
evidence: The code already folds and ranks handoff history, but cumulative session usage cannot show which selected entries caused input. Long/restarted sessions are identifiable in the trace sample, making this a bounded observability-first candidate.
scope: Add offline/diagnostic handoff selection metrics and a fixture corpus before changing the ranking policy. Do not shrink the configured budget or discard corrections, blockers, failed commands, edits, or decisive checks without an outcome comparison.
benefit: Estimated lower repeated input and faster resume turns where a handoff is much smaller than raw history.
measurement: For matched resumes, record candidate/selected character counts, continuation turns, canonical tokens, time to next useful state, and task outcome. Preserve existing handoff behavior as the control.
counter_evidence: The existing rules intentionally protect high-value evidence. A smaller handoff that causes re-reading, wrong changes, or review churn is a regression.

title: Classify repeated verification before suppressing any command
evidence: Selected traces expose repeated tool-command prefixes, while task end facts retain retries and review cycles. The record does not identify whether repetitions were required by changed code, flaky checks, or review findings.
scope: Build an offline classifier/report for repeated commands keyed by commit/head and workflow column. Do not skip hooks, required checks, or reviewer-requested reruns.
benefit: Potentially lower tool wait and subsequent context tokens by avoiding proven duplicate checks; benefit is unquantified.
measurement: Sample repeated commands and label necessity. In a later controlled implementation, compare elapsed tool duration, retry rate, review findings, and task outcomes against the same check policy.
counter_evidence: Repeated checks often establish a flaky-test proof or validate a later change. The audit must not equate repetition with waste.

title: Bound broad tool-result retention with task-aware summaries
evidence: The trace indicators count large stored tool-result payloads. Tool outputs may be echoed into agent context or handoffs, but this database does not record prompt assembly per turn, so causal token savings are untested.
scope: First add a report of large result payloads by tool, role, and outcome. Any later truncation must keep exit status, failing lines, paths, diffs, and an explicit way to retrieve full output.
benefit: Potentially lower input context and handoff size, plus faster model turns on noisy command output.
measurement: Compare prompt/handoff size, canonical token categories, diagnosis success, retry rate, and reviewer findings on matched command-heavy tasks.
counter_evidence: Full output can contain the only failure clue. Do not truncate before a representative trace review demonstrates redundant material.
